headline: Portable, configurable pipelines and GPU basecalling for large-scale sequencing data
label: Scalable Genomic Data Processing
summary: Growing sequencing cohorts and nanopore throughput demand workflows that are both portable across environments and fast on commodity hardware.
synthesis: The common thread is scalable, reproducible execution of sequencing analysis. CBIcall provides a configuration-driven framework that runs standardized variant-calling workflows from FASTQ to VCF via Bash or Snakemake for large sequencing cohorts. MOAflow re-engineers an existing MOA-seq cistrome-occupancy analysis in Nextflow with Docker containers to improve portability. At the compute layer, Openfish and Slorado bring hardware-independent GPU acceleration to nanopore basecalling, with Slorado reported to match Dorado accuracy. What is new is that portability and encapsulated, standardized environments are presented alongside throughput as primary design goals. The evidence here consists of three preprints, so this reflects stated design intent rather than comparative benchmarking across tools.
